 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Boston Bruins return to their home ice on Saturday afternoon to face the Chicago Blackhawks at TD Garden. Boston enters the game with a 9-4-1 record, sitting atop the Atlantic Division and holding second place in the Eastern Conference with 19 points. They need a win badly after a rough road trip that saw them lose to the Carolina Hurricanes and St. Louis Blues.
 Chicago comes into the contest with a 4-9 record, placing them eighth in the Central Division and 15th in the West with eight points. The Black Hawks are also looking to bounce back after a 4-1 loss to the Detroit Red Wings on Thursday. This matchup marks the first of two games between these teams this season, with the second scheduled for New Year's Day in Chicago.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bruins Must Fix Defensive Gaps
 Boston's recent losses have exposed some serious cracks in their own end. The defense has looked particularly weak when opponents attack the area right in front of the net. Per Stanley Cup of Chowder , the team's offense is too dependent on just a few players like Jimmy Hagens or Mark Kastelic if the top six forwards fail to score. This lack of depth is a problem that needs fixing before the season slips away. The young players have shown flashes, but they need to be more consistent to help the team survive tough nights.
 The Bruins cannot afford to relax for even a second against a team that is desperate to get back on track.
 Blackhawks Rely on Bedard Amid Struggles
 Chicago's season has been rough, and their young star Connor Bedard has faced a lot of tough moments. According to Stanley Cup of Chowder, Bedard has been subjected to a level of pressure that is hard to watch. While there are a few players who might make some noise, the overall picture is one of another difficult year under General Manager Kyle Davidson.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Blackhawks do not have the luxury of a shooting binge to make the games interesting. It is just a lot of bad hockey happening on Madison Street. They are not the worst team in the league, but they are close to that line. Boston has to be careful not to let this game get away on them. The Bruins swept the season series last year, winning both games in overtime and regulation. History favors Boston, but the current form of both teams makes this a tricky test.
 The game starts at 1 p.m. ET on Saturday. Fans can catch the action on NESN in Boston or CHSN in Chicago. Radio listeners have 98.5 The Sports Hub in Boston or WGN Radio 720 in Chicago. The Blackhawks need to prove they can compete against a playoff-caliber squad. It is a classic Original Six battle on a spooky Saturday.
